pairs.why: Same saddle in both; B's stitched skirt border reads as a built leather object like the preferred lesson saddles, while A's skirt is a plain moulded slab.
A has the stitched skirt edge that defines the leather panel, while B's skirt is blank and looks more like a toy casting.
B's stitched skirt and strap give the crafted-leather construction the lessons favour; A's skirt and strap are unstitched.
A carries seam stitching on the skirt and strap, so it reads as real tack; B's plain panels look moulded.
B adds clean seam stitching to the skirt and strap with the same smooth finish, so it is closer to the preferred lesson saddles than A's bare panels.
A's stitched skirt and strap make it read as a built object, and the slightly heavier leather grain is still within the real cards' smoothness, while B is unstitched.
B stitches the large skirt border, which defines the saddle's main shape, while A stitches only the strap, so B reads slightly more as a built object.
A outlines the large skirt panel with stitching while B stitches only the narrow strap, so A shows the construction slightly better.
